summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn extends the first ReadIndex line from liveness to index freshness and registers a child question @coalesced_read_index_freshness (parent 708eebc14c4040feb495e11d064001d0-question-0) with its own experiment. The harness admits two ReadIndex requests from a real follower, holds the first heartbeats so the first status stays pending, commits one write through the real MsgProp/MsgApp/MsgAppResp path so the leader's commit index advances between the two admissions, then admits the second request with either the same rctx (probe reuse-rctx) or a distinct one (control) and delivers the real followers' acknowledgments, recording every answer keyed by the rctx it carries. Two comparisons encode the duty that an admission's answer must carry an index at least as new as the commit index observed at that admission: reused rctx (expected violated) and distinct rctx (control, expected holds). Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, the contrast the experiment is built to measure - with a reused rctx the second admission (commit index 2 after the write) receives a single answer carrying index 1, the first admission's recorded index, while with distinct rctxes the answer for the second request carries index 2. The derived comparison value is reported together with both operands (answer_index, committed_at_second_admission), and the question records honestly that whether an application may reuse an rctx is a contract question - release-3.6 forbids it while the same comment says the restriction is lifted from release-3.7 - so the finding is scoped to the producer's index association. The formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
